scope: Finite model of the genuine 4.1.1 allocator over standard declared pandas numeric families, plus the native interval competitor for signed integers. All allocator orders and all nonempty subsets of dtype names are examined. Repeated columns add no tag-set evidence; disjoint initial-letter families are independent in this model. This is source-level reasoning, not empirical prevalence, a proof for arbitrary third-party dtypes, or candidate execution.
important_limitations: The reader numeric universe must equal the historical producer universe; the runtime probe must check this independently.
Actual empty interval serialization must be calibrated against base/official/fixed before alleging a new regression; the released base already has limitations.
The valid scope of this alternate policy is the declared native numeric task domain. No inference about unseen dtype plugins follows.
The one-dtype-one-tag function property is sufficient for exclusion; no universal injectivity theorem is asserted.
